descriptionChirho: Qal intransitive: to experience anger, vexation, or emotional distress oneself, without causing it in another (Arabic cognate سَخِطَ/غَضِبَ confirms intransitive anger; Korean 화를 냈다/분노하리라 and Swahili -kasirika all reflect intransitive state).

Hifil (and theological Piel) causative: to provoke someone — typically God — to anger through sin, idolatry, or disobedience; also God provoking a nation to jealous anger (Arabic أَغَاظَ Form IV causative; Korean 노하게 하다/진노케 하다 'cause to be angry'; Swahili -kasirisha causative of -kasirika).

Hifil/Piel in interpersonal contexts: to vex, taunt, or torment another person through rivalry or provocation, as Peninnah vexed Hannah (Swahili -chokoza 'to tease/taunt' distinct from -kasirisha; Korean 괴롭혔다 'tormented' distinct from 노하게 하다 'made angry').
